idiom_name: Sequelize DataTypes.JSON / JSONB column (object in, object out)
implementation_notes: Sequelize's DataTypes.JSON and DataTypes.JSONB accept a plain object or array and own the stringify/parse boundary, so the entity detail is one attribute of the model and comes back as an object; PostgreSQL gets the binary jsonb type with containment operators and GIN indexes, MySQL/MariaDB/SQLite store JSON natively, and MSSQL has no JSON type (JSON lives in string columns checked with ISJSON). Anything that must be indexed, joined or constrained goes into its own column - the JSON attribute is for the part that is only ever read and written whole.
pitfalls: JSON attributes are mutated in place and Sequelize's change tracking may not flag the update - assign a fresh object (or call changed) after editing.
No validation, defaults or per-field casting exists inside the document, so shape mistakes surface later at read time.
MSSQL has no JSON type, and PostgreSQL json (unlike jsonb) is not indexable; pick the column type deliberately.
